title: Cache-aware attention scaling experiments — field notebook
content:
Goal:
Run a targeted set of experiments to determine how attention kernel selection and KV/prefix cache behavior interact with sequence-length heterogeneity and small-batch traffic. We want actionable knobs for the scheduler so we can reduce p95 tail without regressing throughput or increasing cost per token.

Context and motivation:
- Background: recent customer reports of p95 jumps during mixed short/long request bursts. Existing heuristics prefer FlashAttention for long sequences and a paged/kernel-swap path for extremely long contexts. But we suspect KV-cache locality and fused-op ordering are causing cache thrash and kernel handoff jitter.
- Hypothesis: If we add a cache-awareness signal (per-worker cache hotness + sequence-length histogram) into the kernel routing decision, we can decrease tail latency at small to medium batch sizes (1–8) with minimal throughput loss at larger batches.

Experiment matrix (high level):
1) Baseline: current routing (flash-pref, fallback paged) + standard prefetch thresholds.
2) Prefetch-reduced: reduce prefetch window by 2x to avoid prefetching long KV ranges for short sequences.
3) Cache-aware routing: use live KV hit_rate and recent sequence histogram to prefer kernels that share cache lines with likely next tokens.
4) Fused-op ordering change: try both "compute-first" and "store-first" variants for fused attention ops to see which reduces write amplification.
5) Combined: cache-aware routing + reduced prefetch + store-first fused ops.

Workload definitions:
- Workload A (chat-like): 70% seq<=64, 25% seq 256-512, 5% seq 2048. Batches: 1–4, arrival pattern: Poisson with lambda=150rps on 8GPU node.
- Workload B (long-document serving): 10% seq<=64, 20% seq 512-1024, 70% seq 2048-8192. Batches: 4–16, steady throughput 300rps.
- Workload C (mixed spike): baseline chat distribution but with sudden 10s spikes of 100x long-request fraction every 60s. Small batches.

Config knobs captured per-run (logged):
- kernel_choice_policy: static|latency-first|cache-aware
- prefetch_window: int (tokens)
- fused_op_mode: compute-first|store-first|split
- worker_cache_limit: bytes
- kv_eviction_policy: lru|seg_lru|time_based
- batch_coalescer_timeout_ms

Profiling setup:
- Hardware: 8x A100 40GB (internal lab queue), mixed GPU utilization runs also on T4 for microbenchmark.
- Instrumentation: nvprof-style traces filtered to attention kernels, runtime event logs (enqueue/dequeue), per-request KV cache hit trace (approx sampling 1/20 requests), kernel launch timestamps, cupti counters for DRAM read/write when available.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU occupancy, SM utilization, memory BW, kernel breakdown (flash-attn, paged-attn, fused-attn, prefetcher, memcopy), number of kernel handoffs per request, KV cache hit rate, tail-stall reasons from runtime scheduler.

Representative run summary (Workload A, batch=1, 60s window):
- Baseline:
  p50: 12.2ms, p95: 183ms, p99: 410ms
  tokens/sec: 42k
  kernel breakdown: flash-attn 60% time, fused-attn 25%, prefetcher 8%, memcopy 7%
  KV hit_rate: 18% (sampled)
  observations: frequent kernel handoffs when long request arrives during short-request sequences. Large variance in kernel latency (stdev high).

- Prefetch-reduced:
  p50: 12.0ms, p95: 142ms, p99: 360ms
  tokens/sec: 41.8k (-0.5%)
  KV hit_rate: 16% (prefetch reduced so measured local hits slightly lower)
  observations: fewer unnecessary large prefetches; prefetcher runtime fraction down to 4%. Tail reduced but still visible due to kernel handoffs.

- Cache-aware routing:
  p50: 13.5ms, p95: 88ms, p99: 210ms
  tokens/sec: 40.0k (-4.7%)
  KV hit_rate: 42% (hotspot routing preserves caches)
  kernel_handoffs_per_request: median 1 -> 0 in many short requests
  observations: significant p95 improvement; small throughput loss due to suboptimal kernel choice for long sequences in some cases.

- Fused-op store-first:
  p50: 12.8ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 320ms
  tokens/sec: 41.0k
  DRAM write amplification: -12% vs compute-first (measured by cupti counters)
  observations: store-first reduced memory write storms during bursts, but did not fully eliminate tail because kernel selection still misrouted some requests.

- Combined (cache-aware + pref-reduced + store-first):
  p50: 13.3ms, p95: 72ms, p99: 170ms
  tokens/sec: 39.6k (-5.7%)
  KV hit_rate: 44%
  observations: best tail behaviour observed; throughput loss modest and acceptable for low-latency tier.

Deep dive notes (observations & traces):
- Kernel handoff pattern: most p95 spikes correlate with a long request arriving when worker's KV cache contains many small-seq cached entries. The runtime chooses FlashAttention by latency-first heuristic; FlashAttn warms up kernels and triggers large memory reads for KV ranges, causing L2 thrash leading to other pending short requests suffering high latency.
- Prefetch side effects: aggressive prefetching for long seqs causes large amounts of DRAM traffic; in mixed workloads this increases contention and reduces effective SM utilization for short kernels.
- Cache-aware routing mechanics: using a simple per-worker hotness score (recent KV hits weighted by token size) and a short sequence histogram allowed the router to prefer paged or small-kernel for short sequences even when nominal latency-model favored FlashAttention. This limits disruptive DRAM reads.
- Fused-op ordering: store-first reduces write bursts because we batch writes that would otherwise interleave with compute; compute-first had slightly better raw throughput on long-only workloads but worse mixed-tail.

Quantitative kernel-level breakdown (combined run):
- flash-attn kernel time share: 38%
- paged-attn kernel time share: 22%
- fused-attn: 30%
- prefetcher: 3%
- memcopy/other: 7%
- average kernel handoffs: 0.3 per request

Failure modes and anomalies encountered:
- Measurement bias: sampling KV-hit traces at 1/20 underestimates rare hot-paths. Re-run with deterministic tracing when investigating specific regression.
- Interference: noisy neighbor jobs on shared lab cluster introduced spurious p99 spikes. Isolate on reserved node for final confirmation.
- Edge case: ultra-long sequences (>=16k) still cause rare OOM during prefetch windows; confirmed with synthetic work. Need a guard in prefetcher to cap range with worker memory headroom.

Recommendations (practical):
1) Implement cache-aware routing as an opt-in scheduler mode behind config flag: runtime.router.policy = cache-aware. Start with heuristic thresholds (hotness>0.35 && short_hist_peak>70%) to bias away from FlashAttention for short requests.
2) Default reduce prefetch_window by 2x for mixed workloads; allow enterprise customers to tune when running long-only workloads.
3) Expose fused-op mode as runtime parameter and default to store-first for mixed or low-p95 tiers.
4) Add worker-level KV hotness telemetry to console (histogram + hit_rate) so ops can observe when workers are cache-thrashing.
5) Add a protective cap on prefetch ranges based on free GPU memory to prevent OOMs.

Next experiments (open questions):
- How does cache-aware policy interact with multi-tenant dedicated capacity where tenant isolation may prefer conservative prefetch? Run multitenant sims.
- Can we learn routing decisions (small decision-tree or tiny policy net) from recent request traces to get better throughput/tail balance than static heuristics? A/B test later.
- Explore eviction strategies: seg_lru vs simple lru to better preserve hot long-seq KV segments for long-session chat.
- Microbench: re-run with A30 vs A100 vs T4 to understand cross-arch behavior; FlashAttention sensitivity to SM count observed in micro runs.

Notes to whoever picks this up:
- Start by reproducing Baseline vs Combined using the run_config attached in the PR (linked_artifacts). Use one reserved 8x A100 node and the provided workload generator (scripts/bench/workload_a.py).
- Use deterministic tracing mode when chasing p99. Sampling is useful for quick runs but can hide rare cascades.
- Keep an eye on GPU memory growth during combined runs — store-first fused ops change the allocation patterns slightly.

Appendix: short checklist for the patch that will implement cache-aware routing:
- [ ] Add per-worker rolling KV-hit EMA counter and small-ring sequence histogram (256 buckets).
- [ ] Expose router.policy config and unit tests for decision boundaries.
- [ ] Add unit+integration test: synthetic workload with controlled short/long mix asserting p95 improved by >30% vs baseline on small-batch simulation.
- [ ] Add telemetry plumbing to Console (hotness gauge, sample traces).
- [ ] Documentation: short note on tuning prefetch_window and fused_op_mode for customers.

End of notebook. This is a working doc — expect updates as we run multitenant sims and incorporate feedback from infra team.
